items.title: Mistrial declared in Lindsay Clancy murder case, after jury deadlocks
items.description: The mistrial now puts the murder case - and Clancy's future - in limbo as to whether she will be held criminally liable in the deaths of her three kids.

items.title: Trump's peace envoys to visit Moscow and Kyiv over weekend
items.description: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have led President Donald Trump's efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war - but talks have stalled.

items.title: Europe targeted by spiralling campaign of sabotage - and Russia is the chief suspect
items.description: Germany has blamed Russia for an attack on Leipzig airport but there has been a series of suspicious incidents elsewhere.

items.title: UN votes to adopt new world map to reflect Africa's true size
items.description: The Togo-sponsored resolution was backed by 164 nations - with the US as the only nation to vote against it.

items.title: At least two dead in blast at Bolivia military barracks
items.description: Authorities fear the death toll in Viacha will rise and warn people to stay away from the barracks due to a risk of further explosions.

items.title: Germany's far-right AfD bids for first taste of power in eastern vote
items.description: If it wins an outright majority in Saxony-Anhalt, it would be the first time a far-right party has held state-level power in Germany since World War Two.

items.title: Russia hits Ukrainian security headquarters in drone attack, Zelensky says
items.description: The unmanned aerial vehicle struck without warning in the heart of the Ukrainian capital.

items.title: 'A rare moment of joy': Nepal tunnel rescues bring hope for more flood survivors
items.description: There are still hundreds of workers trapped in a network of tunnels that run along the Trishuli river.

items.title: Tate brothers charged with further trafficking and sex crimes in Romania
items.description: Andrew and Tristan Tate are currently in a Miami jail fighting extradition to the UK over separate charges and deny all the allegations.

items.title: UK support for Falkland Islands 'unwavering' after Argentina restates claims, No 10 says
items.description: The comments come as Argentinian president Javier Milei says the "winds of change" favoured his country's claim on the British overseas territory.

items.title: Argentine couple to return Nazi-looted painting to rightful owner
items.description: The late-baroque Portrait of a Lady was lost for 80 years until it was spotted in photographs of a house for sale near Buenos Aires.

items.title: Body of world's youngest traditional king returns home to Uganda amid succession row
items.description: King Oyo died in the US last week aged 34 after receiving treatment for an aggressive form of cancer.

items.title: How much can Canada fight back in its trade war with the US?
items.description: The US may be the bigger trading partner, but Canada shouldn't be counted out quite yet in the escalating trade fight.

items.title: Flock says its cameras make US safer - so why are they being sabotaged?
items.description: The AI-powered cameras have been vandalised across the US, as citizens object to the growing surveillance network.

items.title: Nepal bet nearly everything on hydropower - the floods show why that's a problem
items.description: More than 10% of Nepal's energy generation capacity was knocked out by last week's floods.

items.title: Is Russia proving better at protecting friends than fighting enemies in West Africa?
items.description: Russian forces were brought in to help defeat jihadists but they also defend the military leadership in Niger.

items.title: How could US-Iran conflict end? Three experts give their views
items.description: After renewed strikes this week, does either side have an exit strategy?

items.title: 'Layer upon layer of miracles' to find tunnel survivors, Nepal rescue adviser tells BBC
items.description: From searching for a buried tunnel entrance to blowing up rocks the size of cars, rescuers had to surmount multiple challenges to reach survivors.

items.title: Kenya's chai lovers are not happy as the nation's cows run dry
items.description: Supermarket shelves are emptying, sellers are rationing supplies and prices are rising.

items.title: 'We expect our sons to be killed,' father of teen shot dead in West Bank tells BBC
items.description: Palestinian teenagers Omar al-Naasan and Khalil Abu Alia were shot dead when Israeli settlers and soldiers entered a village in the occupied West Bank.
